evidence: The user's request, 2026-10-24: "RMC: Displacement Directions page: set the defaul mu=10, smoothing=4x". The page has no mu control: mu is the Resolution control's geodesic frequency nu, its option labelled 'ν=10 (1002)', and 4x is the Smoothing control's value 4 (four neighbour-diffusion passes, shown as 4×). This partly reverses 2026-10-19-directions-auto-resolution for the page: from 2026-10-19 it opened at Auto (the engine's recommendedFrequency, the tiling analyze_displacement_directions reads) and unsmoothed. What stays: every readout under the sphere (the peak, its direction +- the cell radius, its sigma, the map test, the +u/-u asymmetry, the Bingham anisotropy) is requested at smoothing 0 (directionReadoutRequest), so the smoothing redraws only the map. What it costs, measured on dev-thermal-null (thermal motion only, its O flattened across its bond, 512 copies a site): at Auto (nu = 2) the three O sites' map test reads 7.17, 6.30 and 7.13 sigma, at nu = 10 2.32, 2.16 and 2.23 sigma (below the 3 sigma bar); the Bingham anisotropy (9.74, 8.74, 8.83 sigma) and the peak test (below 3 sigma on both) do not change their verdict. The page and the tool therefore agree by default no longer, only when the user picks Auto; a Copilot step's Show in still sets the step's resolution (Auto). Nothing the model is sent changes: analyze_displacement_directions never read the page's settings (it sends no frequency and no smoothing), its description, results and the model-visible snapshots are unchanged, and the displacement-anisotropy skill is not edited. Arm A read the page's defaults from src/directionSettings.js (ARM_A_RULES.DIRECTION_SETTINGS was DIRECTION_DEFAULTS: the resolution, weight, frame and amplitude cut; never the smoothing, which its readout request sets to 0), so it would have followed the page to nu = 10. Arm A is defined by the settings frozen at protocol 2026-10-24.6, not by the page's current defaults; armA.js pins them. Arm A on the dev set after the change (no --final, a scratch file): all 45 records identical to validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json apart from their commit field (protocol 2026-10-24.6; means A 0.8135, A+ 0.9516, D 1.0 before and after; no case moved). The test set was not run. Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
proposed_fix: src/directionSettings.js: DIRECTION_DEFAULTS, the page's opening settings, is { frequency: 10, weight: 'count', frame: 'cartesian', minQuantile: 0, smoothing: 4 }; FREQUENCY_OPTIONS keeps 'auto' and 10; directionReadoutRequest (smoothing 0) and directionMapRequest (the page's smoothing) are unchanged, so the page opens with two requests landing together, the readout at nu = 10 unsmoothed and the map at nu = 10 smoothed 4x. The Resolution help no longer calls Auto the default. validation/armA.js: ARM_A_RULES.DIRECTION_SETTINGS is its own frozen constant, { frequency: 'auto', weight: 'count', frame: 'cartesian', minQuantile: 0, smoothing: 0 } (arm A is defined by the settings frozen at protocol 2026-10-24.6, not by the page's current defaults; armA.js pins them), so no record, baseline, protocol or freeze changes. analyze_displacement_directions is untouched (Auto, unsmoothed). The known-answer test of 2026-10-19 now compares the page at Auto (arm A's settings) with the tool, and its renamed tests are repointed in that record. Docs: AGENTS.md, docs/algorithms (displacement-directions, copilot-validation, ai-assistant), ALGORITHMS.md and ROADMAP.md say the page opens at nu = 10, smoothed 4x; a change fragment. Left open for the user: the displacement-anisotropy skill still says the page opens at Auto (its known failure modes), for the skill fact-sync (the skills are what the model reads, so not edited here). Approved by the user, 2026-10-24.
